chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, who said:
I saw Musa (peace be upon him) offering condolences before the burial and after it.
ai.seo_question: When should condolences be offered according to the example of Musa (AS)?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the reliable chain of Ibn Abi Umayr and Hisham ibn al-Hakam, highlights the timeless etiquette of *ta'ziyah* (condolences) by citing the practice of Prophet Musa (peace be upon him). It establishes that offering comfort to the bereaved is a recommended act of piety that remains valid both prior to and following the burial, reinforcing its status as a continuous social obligation in Shia jurisprudence.
